raw_response:
I am 71 years old this year, and I have been farming since I was 20. I only finished primary school, so everything I know about farming I learned from my father and from doing it myself year after year. I don't trust those people from the agricultural station much — last time they told me to cut back on fertilizer, my wheat yield dropped, and nobody paid me back for the loss.

I have 10.5 mu of land, just me and my wife at home now. The children are all working in the city. I divide my land into two pieces. The big piece, 7 mu, I plant wheat in October and millet after I harvest the wheat in early June. That is what I have always done. The other piece, 3.5 mu, I plant spring maize in April because that land is a bit sandier and maize grows better there.

For the wheat on the 7 mu, I buy improved seed from the shop in town — Luyuan 502 or Jimai 22, whatever they have that year. I use 30 jin of seed per mu, so I need about four bags for the whole piece. I rotary till the field before planting in October. At planting, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 50 kg of 15-15-15. Then in March, when the wheat starts to turn green, I topdress with urea. I use about 40 jin of urea per mu. I know it sounds like a lot, but I would rather waste a little fertilizer than lose yield. A bad harvest means I lose thousands of yuan. Wasting one bag of urea is only 100-something yuan. I irrigate three times: once in winter if it does not snow, once when the wheat is jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once after planting, and I spray for insects and disease if I see them — usually twice more. If the weather is normal, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

For the millet, after I cut the wheat in early June, I plant millet right away. I do not have much time — if you delay, the frost comes before the millet is ready. I use an improved variety, Huangjinmiao or whatever the seed dealer has. The seeds are tiny — only 2 jin per mu. I do not till much, sometimes I just run the machine quickly or plant no-till if I am in a hurry. Millet does not need much fertilizer. I put about 30 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and that is usually enough. If it rains well, I do not irrigate, but if it is dry when the millet is heading, I water once from the well. I spray herbicide once, and maybe insecticide once if there are bugs. I expect about 350 kg per mu.

For the maize on the 3.5 mu piece, I plant Denghai 605 hybrid seed in April. Hybrid seed is expensive — about 60 yuan per bag — and I need about 5 jin per mu. I rotary till in spring and put compound fertilizer in the planting holes. Then when the maize is knee-high, I side-dress with urea — about 40 jin per mu. I irrigate twice, once when it is growing fast and once when it tassels. I spray herbicide after planting, and if I see corn borers, I spray insecticide once. Spring maize does not yield as much as summer maize, but I expect about 550 kg per mu.

Everything is done by me and my wife. We hire the combine for wheat harvest, and I rent the rotary tiller from the village machine owner. We use our well for all the irrigation. I watch what Old Wang and the others do — if they put more fertilizer this year, I do too. You cannot be the one who tries to save money and then ends up with the worst crop in the village.
